plan: This mechanism functions like a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), since my exit price acts as my bid, and the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding truthfully (equal to my value) is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Bidding higher risks negative profit if I win at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my true value of $35.

Since the sealed bid acts as my exit price in the ascending clock auction, and the winner pays the second-highest bid (a second-price auction structure), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. Bidding my value ensures I win whenever it's profitable (my value exceeds the price) and never overpay, since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win. There's no incentive to shade or inflate my bid.

This is effectively a second-price auction: my sealed bid acts as my maximum willingness to pay, and I'll win only if others' bids are lower, paying the second-highest bid. Bidding my true value ($48) is the dominant strategy—it ensures I win whenever profitable (value exceeds price) and never overpay, since I only pay the second-highest bid if I win.
